newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian official blasts investment focus.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian official blasts investment focus.

text.p: The governor of the Palestinian Monetary Authority on Monday blasted banks in the West Bank and Gaza over investments abroad, demanding they focus on investing at home.

Fouad Bseiso told businessmen and bankers in the West Bank town of Nablus that out of an estimated $1.8 billion in local deposits, more than $1.0 billion was invested abroad compared with $300 million lent to Palestinians in the PLO-ruled West Bank and Gaza Strip.

"We are against investment of this volume abroad. It is a damned phenomenon and we are trying to slow it down," Bseiso said. "We are trying to raise the volume of local loans because we want these banks to contribute to local investment and development," he said.
The Palestinian Monetary Authority acts as a central bank for the self-rule areas, but does not issue currency.
The Jordanian dinar, the Israeli shekel and the U.S. dollar are the main currencies in circulation in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Palestinian financial experts said that 17 banks, mostly Jordanian-based, have opened branches in the West Bank and Gaza Strip since the Palestinian Authority took charge of parts of the two regions in 1994 under a self-rule deal with Israel.

Yousef al-Bazyan, regional director of the Amman, Jordan-based Cairo-Amman Bank, said the absence of loan guarantees and lack of an investment climate were among the reasons for the low ratio of loans to deposits.
"Unfortunately, there is no suitable investment climate until now to encourage loans," Bazyan said.
